title: History matters only through the present state it produces

statements.text: The result does not make history unimportant. Learning, development, recurrent activity, computation and sensory processing may be indispensable in producing the present state, and that state holds memory traces, synaptic changes, field configurations and stored data. What is ruled out is that having undergone a process counts again once the present state is fixed.

sources.quote: This conclusion does not imply that history is unimportant in the study of conscious systems.
The remaining response is the corollary: history matters only through the present physical state it produces.
